title: Lower Shawneetown: A Shawnee Town in Greenup County
summary: In Greenup County, Lower Shawneetown was a major Shawnee town of the mid-1700s in the Ohio Valley, shown as Lower Shawneetown on English maps.
bodyMarkdown:
Long before stations dotted the Bluegrass, a major Shawnee town stood in what is now Greenup County. English maps called it Lower Shawneetown; it may have been a Chillicothe, a principal place of the Chalahgawtha division.

By 1751 eyewitnesses put the population around 1,200. It was a diplomatic hub and the western end of Pennsylvania's southern deerskin trade, with English trading houses in town. Between April and November 1758, as the French and Indian War made the river mouth unsafe, the Shawnee moved north. Kentucky archaeology still holds Fort Ancient pottery mixed with mid-1700s European trade goods from the Bentley and related sites in Greenup County.
Source: [https://archaeology.ky.gov/Find-a-Site/Pages/Lower-Shawneetown.aspx](https://archaeology.ky.gov/Find-a-Site/Pages/Lower-Shawneetown.aspx)
